name: sp3-sp2: tetraphenylmethane nodes and phenylene struts, large
description: An sp3-sp2 network in which every sp3 carbon is a pre-built tetraphenylmethane node, so it always carries four phenyl (sp2) arms, joined strictly through 1,4-phenylene (node arm to phenylene only, cp-cp 1.485 A): struts C-(C6H4)3-C, a diamond-like topology made amorphous, with the sp3 centres the only breaks in conjugation (GAFF 1.81, params/gaff_paf). Built large: a 60 A cell with 8 tetraphenylmethane seeds, then ten passes, each growing 60 blocks, joining clusters twice, zipping and a rigid-body optimisation with dihedrals. Then a closing phase: three rounds of a wide zip (3.0 A, 110 degrees, clash-checked) and an all-atom (flexible) optimisation, which closes rings, including across the periodic boundary so the framework spans the cell, and lets the blocks flex (docs/closing.md). Then Poreblazer on a 0.3 A grid, and liminal's pi-conduction analysis, with through-space couplings between stacked rings (conjugated domains, Hückel gap, conductance with and without tunnelling through the sp3 nodes; needs liminal). Sized for a Slurm node (resources). See docs/sp3-sp2-networks.md.
